overview: Hypothyroidism occurs when the thyroid gland produces too little thyroid hormone, which slows metabolism. It can cause tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, hair thinning, low mood, and a slow heart rate. Common causes include autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto's), iodine imbalance, thyroid surgery, and some medicines. It is usually diagnosed with blood tests and is highly treatable.
